findings.summary: crates/athena-core/src/scope_guard.rs is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: A change job's reader loses the other studies whenever the request text selects one system id. This contradicts the request and criterion 2, and the trigger is a plain text match that fires often.
findings.evidence: The request says "change jobs still see all studies", and criterion 2 says "a change job's snapshots hold both". The reader chooses the capability (reading.rs:719-730, capability set at :817), so read_once (:551) cannot know the job type. The plan therefore hides on any request that names exactly one configured system id. Its test 2(d) asserts "the Reader lacks the other studies" for a change job. In this repository, change requests about the firstmate study, its rules tests or its fixtures name "firstmate" (it appears in HISTORY.txt subjects). Once studies/hermes-agent exists, every such change request would hide that study from its reader. The plan puts this to the user instead of designing around it. Fix: Make the reader that produced a change job's accepted reading see the full tree. Two options: (a) if read_once used a non-empty hidden list and the reading's capability is not "study", discard that reading and read once more with an empty list, and accept that second reading; or (b) hide in the reader only when the request uses the systems schema's explicit selector form (whatever step 1 finds, such as a dedicated line), not a bare id somewhere in the text. Change test 2(d) to assert that the change job's accepted-reading reader holds both studies, and say what happens if the reader returns study on the full re-read.

findings.summary: Criterion 1's firstmate half uses a made-up SHA, not the SHA in the real studies/firstmate-work-handling/pin.json.
findings.evidence: The plan commits "a 40-hex SHA literal in the test ... the test never reads the real studies/ file". The request says firstmate "still pins the SHA in its pin.json", and that real pin.json gives repository_url https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate.git. With a literal, the test still passes if the real pin.json and athena.toml's firstmate repo_url stop matching, so the test does not check the real configuration. Fix: Build the fixture's pin.json from include_str!("../../../studies/firstmate-work-handling/pin.json") and assert that the request carries that file's sha. If this is avoided on purpose (the test would fail in a Hermes study agent's hidden view), say so and add an assertion that the real pin.json's repository_url equals firstmate's configured repo_url.

findings.summary: Two rows of the commit-shape table have no test: an intervention commit on studies/<other> and a records commit in the branch.
findings.evidence: The table says an intervention commit already on the base that touches studies/<other> stays in the base tree and lands unchanged. The criterion-3 repository holds only the initial studies/a and studies/b plus README. change_list now filters what lands (candidate.rs:34 applies change entries to the full base tree), but no fixture has a later base commit under studies/a or a records/ commit. Fix: In the criterion-3 fixture, add a base commit that edits studies/a after it was created (an intervention) and a commit under records/. Then assert that studies/a in HEAD equals the intervention's bytes and that the landed diff names only README.md.

summary: I checked the plan against the snapshot by reading code; I ran nothing. Most of it holds up. Snapshot::create/materialize (snapshot.rs:59-110, 257-285) work the way the plan assumes. Hidden directories never enter the snapshot repository, so they cannot show up as 'D'. All change_list callers are in athena-core and are listed in the dependents. verifier_snapshot (verification.rs:447-470) can be rebuilt at verify_dir before candidate_view (:58), and ctx.job.job.pin is set at dispatch (mod.rs:1088, 1239) before any agent snapshot is made. The test at drain.rs:5017 sits under #[cfg(test)], so the producer's `cargo build` still works in the hidden view. The base lacks the systems schema (no `systems` in config.rs; pin_repo reads only `[capabilities.study]`), and step 1 stops the producer in that case, which is correct. One design problem remains. The reader picks the capability itself, so the plan hides other studies from any request whose text selects one system id. Its own test 2(d) then asserts that a change job's reader lacks the other studies. That breaks the request's "change jobs still see all studies" and criterion 2's "a change job's snapshots hold both", and it fires on plain text mentions such as "firstmate" in ordinary change requests. The two minor points: criterion 1 pins a made-up SHA instead of the one in the real pin.json, and the landing test's repository has no realistic branch history.
